name: Benito Mussolini
kicker: Italy’s Fascist dictator · Allied with Hitler through most of World War II
briefing: Benito Mussolini sent his Blackshirt followers marching on Rome in 1922 and pressured the king into making him prime minister, then built Europe’s first Fascist dictatorship. As _Il Duce_ [“eel DOO-chay”], “the Leader,” he invaded Ethiopia and allied with Adolf Hitler to lead Italy through most of World War II. Italian partisans captured and executed him in April 1945, days before Hitler’s own death.

tossups.p: This man signed the Lateran Treaty with Pope Pius XI in 1929, recognizing Vatican City’s independence. Six years earlier, the Acerbo Law had guaranteed his political party a two-thirds majority in Italy’s parliament.
tossups.r: German commandos rescued this man from a mountain hotel in the 1943 Gran Sasso Raid, after which he led the puppet Republic of Salò. For 10 points, name this Fascist dictator of Italy, nicknamed “Il Duce.”

tossups.p: This man’s Blackshirts marched on Rome in 1922, pressuring King Victor Emmanuel III into naming him prime minister. His government bombarded the Greek island of Corfu in 1923 after an Italian general was murdered.
tossups.r: This man invaded Ethiopia in 1935, forcing Emperor Haile Selassie into exile. For 10 points, name this Fascist dictator who allied with Adolf Hitler during World War II.

tossups.p: As a young socialist, this man edited the newspaper _Avanti!_ [“ah-VAHN-tee”] before breaking with the party over Italy’s entry into World War I. He later promoted a “Battle for Wheat” and a “Battle for Births” to boost Italian farming and population.
tossups.r: King Victor Emmanuel III dismissed this man in 1943 after the Allied invasion of Sicily. For 10 points, name this Fascist leader who was then rescued by German commandos in the Gran Sasso Raid.

tossups.p: This man invaded Albania in 1939, forcing King Zog into exile. His Fascist followers had earlier murdered the socialist critic Giacomo Matteotti [“mah-teh-OT-tee”] in 1924.
tossups.r: After Italian partisans captured this man in April 1945, he was executed along with his companion Clara Petacci near Lake Como. For 10 points, name this dictator who led Italy’s Fascist government and allied with Nazi Germany.

tossups.p: This man’s forces fought a long colonial war to control Libya in the 1920s. In 1935, he joined Britain and France in the short-lived Stresa Front, briefly standing against German expansion before switching sides.
tossups.r: This man led the puppet Italian Social Republic after being freed in the Gran Sasso Raid. For 10 points, name this Fascist dictator executed by partisans in 1945.

tossups.p: This man’s government issued the Manifesto of Race and passed antisemitic laws in 1938, following Nazi Germany’s lead. Pietro Badoglio replaced this man as prime minister after King Victor Emmanuel III had him arrested in 1943.
tossups.r: This man was then rescued from a mountain hotel by German commandos in the Gran Sasso Raid. For 10 points, name this Italian dictator nicknamed “Il Duce.”

tossups.r: This man’s regime invaded Ethiopia in 1935 and exiled its emperor, Haile Selassie. For 10 points, name this Fascist dictator, known as “Il Duce,” who allied with Hitler in World War II.

tossups.r: German paratroopers soon rescued this man in the Gran Sasso Raid, after which he led a German-backed puppet state in northern Italy. For 10 points, name this Italian Fascist leader executed in 1945.

tossups.p: Early in his career, this man edited the socialist newspaper _Avanti!_ before turning against socialism and founding the National Fascist Party. His Fascist followers killed the socialist politician Giacomo Matteotti in 1924.
tossups.r: This man’s Blackshirts had marched on Rome in 1922 to put him in power. For 10 points, name this dictator of Fascist Italy, known as “Il Duce.”

tossups.r: Italian partisans captured and executed this man in April 1945. For 10 points, name this Fascist dictator who had invaded Ethiopia and forced out its emperor, Haile Selassie.

trap.title: Il Duce, king, or Hitler?
trap.body: Real packets prompt on “Il Duce” before his name is read, so buzzing with just the nickname only earns a second chance, not the points. Players also confuse him with King Victor Emmanuel III, who appointed and later dismissed him but was Italy’s actual head of state, and with his ally Adolf Hitler, who led Germany, not Italy.
trap.fix: If the clues describe Italy’s government, the Blackshirts, or “Il Duce,” give his full name. “Victor Emmanuel” wants the king who hired and fired him; “Hitler” wants the German dictator he allied with.
trap.line: Real answer line: Benito Mussolini (prompt on “Il Duce” before read)
